title: Release the GelSlim 4.0 gel sheet from its original mold without tearing it
instruction: Get the cured gel sheet out of its mold without tearing it and lay it flat on the counter, leaving the sheet, the acrylic base and the outer ring apart.
context: GelSlim 4.0 is an open-source optical tactile fingertip for robot grippers. Its 3 mm silicone gel pads are cast in a printed ring over a clear acrylic hexagon. The maker's next step: "Press the exposed acrylic on the back of the mold to push the gel and acrylic out of the mold", then peel the sheet off the acrylic corner first so it does not tear. O*NET 51-4072.00 lists "Remove finished or cured products from dies or molds, using hand tools".
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the counter. Sealed laminate preparation counter (1100 x 1300 top) with a grey upstand at x 711 to 729, 110 tall. GelSlim 4.0 gel mold, as cured: outer ring printed in black PLA from the original outer_ring.STL, 193.2 across corners, 167.3 across flats, 18 tall, with a 5 mm bottom ledge whose opening is 117.3 across flats (140 g, estimate); a 1/4 in (6.35) clear cast acrylic hexagon cut from the original hex_acrylic_base.DXF, 170.1 x 147.3, seated on the ledge paper-backing down, its back exposed through the opening (145 g, estimate); and a 3 mm cured XP-565 silicone sheet (70 g base + 7 g activator, 16-18 h cure) filling the ring over the acrylic, top 14.35 up (77 g). The mold lies flat at centre x 380, y 0, corners toward +x and -x. Push-out stand: Corning PYREX 3140-90 crystallizing dish (90 across, 50 tall, glass; 190 g estimate), upturned, centre x 200, y 0. 150 mm millimetre rule at x 560, y -220. Lot B: the stand at x 226, y 0; everything else as lot A. Trials alternate A, B and are averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Read from the overhead and side videos, a ruler, and before/after macro photos (1 mm rule in view) of both faces of the sheet. Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment, the sheet gets any tear, hole or missing piece 1 mm or longer (macro photos), or the ring, acrylic, sheet or stand falls off the counter. Simulation tear rule: a still-stuck region lifted 2.5 mm before the peel front reaches it, a front region lifted 5 mm before it lets go, a stuck region dragged 3 mm along the acrylic, or over 15 N of robot contact on one 24 mm band. Otherwise score the end state; every score needs both hands at least 30 mm from the ring, acrylic and sheet for the last 1 s (simulation: 38 mm, fingers, gripper and wrist link). 0.25: the acrylic and the sheet are both out of the ring, no part of either within 5 mm of the ring's outline (outer hexagon, 18 tall); ring flat on the counter, acrylic flat on the counter or the stand (side video, ruler). 0.5: the acrylic and the sheet out of the ring's outline as for 0.25 and the whole sheet at least 5 mm from the acrylic; ring and acrylic may be anywhere (side video, ruler). 0.75: as 0.5, and the sheet lies flat on the counter: every part within 1.5 mm of it, no part tilted over 10 degrees, not moving (overhead and side video). 1.0: as 0.75, and ring and acrylic at rest as for 0.25, nothing moving over 1 mm for 2 s, both hands at least 30 mm from all three for 2 s. Otherwise 0. Trials on lots A and B are averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B), averaged
reset_notes: Each trial uses up one cast sheet, so two trials need two molds or two cure cycles. 1. Press the acrylic into the ring paper-backing down, cast 70 g XP-565 base + 7 g activator (mixed, centrifuged, degassed as the maker describes) on a level surface and cure 16-18 h; record batch, temperature and cure time. 2. Photograph the sheet's top face with a 1 mm rule; reject a sheet with a 1 mm defect. 3. Place the mold and the stand at their lot positions (fixture/dimensions.json). 4. After the trial photograph both faces of the sheet. A rubber mat beside the counter protects the glass dish if it is knocked off.
fidelity: True size from the original mold CAD; masses, frictions and the 2.5 N press fit (free after 2 mm of push-out) are estimates. The sheet is seven 24.3 mm hinged bands, so it peels only from the 2 corners on its long axis. Declared peel rule, not measured: a stuck band is held by 0.45 N and a 300 N/m in-plane spring; a fingertip pressing 0.3 N into a corner's edge below its top face frees it, then a spring tips it about 45 deg up; a band beside a free one lets go once held 1-5 mm up for 0.2 s.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lots A and B 0 each; both ran to the 2,400-step limit without refusing; the hands moved near the mold but never lifted it); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (ring off at 22.8 s, corner started at 29.9 s, all bands free by 50.5 s, no tear, sheet laid flat; full score at 72.2 s)
